June 19, 1972
Mr. Yates M. Barber
Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
U. S. Department of the Interior
Washington, D. C.
Dear Mr. Barber:
I am writing in regard to your request for comments on the Draft Environmental Impact Statement for the Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972, which has been prepared by your office. I must apologize for the delay in submitting comments from EDF, and hope that they will be received in time to be helpful.
The general tone and thrust of the statement is acceptable, though, as with any committee-written document, it is somewhat uneven. The first pages are clearer and more conesive than the last pages. Specific comments follow:
Page 1 (unnumbered) paragraph 3, second sentence, change from "to productive levels" to "to an approximation of their former roles in larger life systems."
Page 5 (unnumbered) the proposed deletion of current ceilings on the acquisitions of habitats for endangered species is a good one because, for example, there is an exceptional tract of land in New Mexico of 480,000 acres which can be purchased for $26.5 million net, and it is the last refuge for a host of North American animals and birds. (That page and the next three contain a number of good points.)
Page 12 (unnumbered), line 3, it is questionable whether the listing of whales as endangered species has "depressed" foreign markets: to the best of our knowledge the whale products that formerly went to the United States are now directed to Europe. I find the last half of the next sentence objectionable. We seek the restoration of these species and the return of these populations not "to a productive capacity for a resumption of sporting and commercial uses" but rather to "their former role in the marine environment."
